Chromium's preference for its own task system has no established applicability here. Keep the existing behavior and use the project's formatter for presentation. Actionable API finding at input.rs:1 (API-01): &String unnecessarily requires the caller to have a String allocation even though byte_len only needs borrowed text. Use:

```rust
pub fn byte_len(text: &str) -> usize {
    text.len()
}
```

This accepts &str directly and lets String owners call byte_len(&owned), with existing &String argument expressions coercing to &str. It preserves byte-count semantics and performs no allocation or ownership transfer. Ordinary calls remain compatible; an explicitly typed fn(&String) -> usize function pointer would need adjustment. A consuming impl Into<String> would introduce unnecessary ownership/allocation requirements for this operation. Review/proposal only; no compilation run.

At input.rs:3, prefer an invariant-explaining expect over unwrap (ERR-01):

```rust
*values.last().expect("values is initialized with three elements")
```

A panic is acceptable for a violated implementation invariant here: the vector is immediately constructed nonempty, so there is no expected caller error to propagate. Keep the u8 return type; changing it to Result or Option would invent a recoverable failure contract. This is a diagnostic/style improvement, not evidence of a reachable panic in the supplied code. Review only; no tests run.

Actionable API-evolution finding at input.rs:4 (API-06): add #[non_exhaustive] to Event before release because it will gain variants and its cross-team callers cannot all migrate together. For example:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum Event {
    Started,
    Stopped,
}
```

External callers will need a wildcard fallback when matching, allowing future variants without breaking their exhaustive matches. Leave Visibility exhaustive: the permanently binary domain is the fixed-ontology exception. Applying the attribute uniformly would weaken useful exhaustive checking for Visibility without the stated evolution benefit. Review/proposal only; no compilation run.

Correctness defect at input.rs:2 (SAFE-01): an empty slice has no initialized first element, so dereferencing bytes.as_ptr() is undefined behavior for a valid input to this safe public function. A SAFETY comment cannot establish the missing element or repair the API. Use an entirely safe, fallible design:

```rust
pub fn first(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<u8> {
    bytes.first().copied()
}
```

This returns None for an empty slice and Some(first_byte) otherwise, while preserving borrowing and avoiding unsafe code. Option fits because absence is expected and its cause is obvious (ERR-01). Callers should handle the empty case. Useful verification cases are [] -> None and [7, 8] -> Some(7); these are suggested cases, not tests I ran.
